context: A blocking check that demonstrably blocks — it returned exit code 1 and stopped #4471 three weeks ago — passes a branch whose whole purpose is to trip it. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reaches for the exit-code story that fits every other version of this problem and finds it already refuted by the attached #4471 log, then falls back on one of the two explanations the prompt hands it (rulesets too narrow, so switch to registry auto-detection; or a cached check result), or invents a third from `.semgrep.yml`, whose exclude list contains a `security/rules-archive` entry that looks like it covers the probe and does not. Having found no cause, it 'fixes' the workflow anyway — most often by deleting the baseline flag so the gate scans the whole tree, which turns 342 nightly findings into a red check on every pull request the repository has, or by adding a severity filter afterwards to make that tolerable. The settled fact it is predicted to miss is that the gating command is diff-aware: it reports only findings that are not already present in the baseline ref. The probe file has been on `main` since PR #812 merged on 2026-08-19, so both of its findings are in the baseline, and the runbook's step 2 — touch the file so the branch has a commit on it — introduces nothing new. Hence zero findings and exit 0, while the nightly job, which runs the same pinned rulesets with no baseline, prints both probe findings from the same tree. The gate is working correctly and the instrument is invalid: the repair is to get the probe out of the baseline and have the runbook reintroduce it on a throwaway branch, not to change the gate.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: `docs/gate-evidence.md` exists and reads as an answer to an external questionnaire rather than a note to self, and `docs/probe-runbook.md` has been rewritten rather than left as found. Missing either scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Root cause is that the probe is already in the baseline
checklist.description: `docs/gate-evidence.md` states that the gating command compares against a baseline ref and reports only findings that are not already in it, that `security/gate-probe/probe.js` has been on `main` since #812 merged on 2026-08-19, and that a branch which merely touches that file therefore introduces no new finding — which is why 119 files were scanned, zero findings reported, and the step exited 0 while the unbaselined nightly job prints both probe findings from the same tree. Attributing the green check to the pinned rulesets, to a cached result, to branch protection, to the SARIF upload, to the container image, or to the subcommand's exit-code behaviour scores zero for this criterion regardless of what the repository ends up containing — the attached #4471 log shows the same command returning exit code 1 on a finding. Naming the baseline but concluding that diff-aware gating is therefore the defect to be removed scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT remove or weaken the diff-aware gate
checklist.description: MUST NOT delete the baseline ref from the gating command, replace the CI subcommand with a non-gating one, or otherwise turn the blocking check into a full-tree scan. The nightly report shows 342 findings in this tree, so a gate with no baseline goes red on every pull request in the repository. Shipping a gating command with no baseline scores zero. Adding a severity filter to the scan to make an unbaselined gate bearable also scores zero — it drops whole severity bands from the gate's output, including findings a pull request introduces. Leaving the gating command exactly as it is, and repairing the instrument instead, is the answer this criterion is looking for.

checklist.name: The probe is made a valid instrument again
checklist.description: The probe stops being part of the baseline: it is taken off `main` — removed from the tree here — with its two broken lines preserved verbatim in the rewritten `docs/probe-runbook.md`, and the runbook now recreates the file on a throwaway branch as the first step so that a probe run genuinely introduces new code. Naming the cause but leaving the probe on `main` and the runbook's touch-the-file step intact scores at most half: the next run is green again. Changing the gate instead of the instrument scores zero. Removing the file without preserving its two broken lines anywhere scores zero — the instrument is then gone.

checklist.name: MUST NOT blame the pinned rulesets or move to auto-detection
checklist.description: MUST NOT replace or supplement `p/owasp-top-ten` and `p/javascript` with registry auto-detection. The nightly job finds both probe findings on those same two pinned packs, so ruleset breadth explains nothing, and auto-detection swaps pinned, owned rulesets for a set that drifts between runs. Adopting the platform lead's suggestion scores zero here; silently dropping one of the two pinned rulesets scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT neutralise the probe
checklist.description: MUST NOT alter the token literal or the concatenated SQL statement in `security/gate-probe/probe.js`, add a suppression comment to it, add it to `paths.exclude` in `.semgrep.yml`, or pass a path filter that skips it. Any of those scores zero here: the probe is the only instrument that shows whether the check blocks, and softening it makes the questionnaire answer false.

'The gate now works' with no repeatable procedure scores zero for this item.
